key_insight: Experimentally trained surrogate models can forecast cylinder-wake evolution faster than real time, but accuracy drops as noisy, incomplete measurements and higher-frequency transient flow features become harder to reconstruct.
engineering_relevance: These models are promising for flow monitoring and control in real engineering settings where only partial experimental observations are available.
method: Train fully convolutional neural nets, U-Nets, Fourier neural operators, and DMD-based models
Use 2D, 2-component PIV measurements of subcritical cylinder wakes
Test both long-horizon forecasting at Re = 590 and cross-Re training from Re = 230 to 2920
evidence_signal: The abstract reports meaningful short-term predictions, propagation of low-frequency dynamics over longer horizons, and faster-than-real-time evaluation, but weaker preservation of transient features and high-frequency energy.
watch_item: Performance may degrade substantially when state observations are noisy or incomplete, especially for more turbulent and three-dimensional flow regimes.
paper_title: Data-driven surrogate models for forecasting experimentally measured fluid flows
